Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Nimbus is excited about Redwood as a replacement for our current inference stack. Before we proceed to a commercial term sheet, procurement and InfoSec have asked for a few non-standard items that will need to be included in the private/VPC contract and SOW. I wanted to put them on your radar and understand what approvals we need on your side. High level: we need (1) named-data residency in us-east-1 only, (2) KMS integration with our HSM for key wrapping, (3) a short-term on-prem audit node for our auditors (2 weeks access, read-only; no code execution), and (4) a 7-year retention window for logs related to access and model inputs for compliance reporting.

I attached a requirements matrix (nimbus_map_requirements.pdf). We also anticipate a request for a contract credit tied to the operational burden (they asked informally for ~15% concession during the first 12 months). Can you confirm who on your side needs to sign off and whether any of these are immediate blockers? Procurement would like a single point of contact to close the SOW redlines.

Best,
Samira

Thanks Tessa — quick read and initial thoughts:
- Residency: us-east-1 pinning is straightforward for hosted/private routing; we need to lock the region in the SOW and add a migration protection clause. No exec sign-off required for region pinning.
- KMS/HSM: KMS integration (customer-managed keys with HSM wrap) is doable but will require our security team to validate the key exchange pattern and an Ops runbook; expect a 3–4 week onboarding window. Recommend we add a KMS attestation milestone in the SOW.
- Audit node: allowing an on-prem node for auditors is sensitive. We can offer a read-only audit appliance (VM snapshot with network egress disabled) but Legal will likely push back on scope of data exposed.
- 7-year retention: this is the biggest risk. Our default retention for access/model-input logs is 1 year (configurable), but 7 years triggers compliance and storage-cost buckets and may require a separate archival workflow. Realistic ask: if Nimbus will commit to a 36-month retention for a premium + separate archival S3 cost pass-through, we can accept; 7yr needs exec approval and an updated storage SOW.

On the pricing credit: 15% first-year concession is a material ask for Dedicated/Private deals. If Legal can craft constrained audit access language and Nimbus accepts a 36-month retention with a confirmed pass-through for archival fees, we might be able to do a 10% first-year operational credit with the caveat of a minimum 12-month commitment and an onboarding fee to cover the KMS integration. Anything outside that needs Deal Desk + Exec sign-off.

I'll sync with Security and Ops and can provide a redline by EOD. For now I'm flagging two exec decision points: (1) approval for >36 month retention up to 7 years, and (2) approval for >10% first-year commercial concession.

— Karthik

Samira / Nimbus team — thanks for detailing requirements and for your patience while we reviewed internally. Attaching a clean SOW excerpt below and a separate redline to your draft (see draft_sow_redlines.docx). Key points and changes we require: 

1) Audit appliance: We can provide a secured, read-only audit VM image with network egress disabled and session recordings for auditors. Access will be provided under a supervised remote session model — auditors cannot export raw datasets or execute arbitrary queries. Any deviation (file export, code execution) will require a separate, time-boxed legal and security process.

2) Data residency: Redwood will host primary inference workloads in us-east-1 only for the scope of this agreement. We will include a non-migration covenant for the initial 24 months, after which region migration will require 90 days' notice.

3) KMS/HSM: We will support customer-managed keys with HSM wrap via a validated key-wrap protocol. Before keys are accepted into production, Nimbus must pass our KMS attestation checklist (milestone in SOW).

4) Retention: We cannot agree to 7-year active retention of raw model inputs due to regulatory and privacy risk. Proposed compromise: 36 months of active retention for model inputs and access logs, with up to 7 years of hashed/archived audit traces (non-reversible) retained in a secure cold archive for compliance only, subject to a documented access request process and cost pass-through. Any request for raw data retrieval beyond 36 months will be evaluated separately and require exec approval.

Commercial ask: based on the operational lift for KMS integration and the bespoke archival workflow, Deal Desk is comfortable offering a 10% first-year operational credit if Nimbus accepts the 36-month/7-year-archival compromise and agrees to a 12-month minimum committed term with cost pass-through for cold storage. Any increase to 15% or acceptance of 7yr raw retention must be escalated to an executive approval chain (VP Commercial + Legal sign-off).

Next steps: Tessa — can you confirm whether Nimbus will accept the 36mo active / 7yr archival compromise and the 12-month minimum? If yes, I'll prepare a clean SOW excerpt and revised commercial term sheet for signature. If they push for 7yr raw retention or a 15% concession, we'll need to escalate to VP-level approval.

Regards,
Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference
